newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia Hong Leong Bank in rights issue.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Hong Leong Bank in rights issue.

text.p: Malaysia's Hong Leong Bank Bhd has proposed a rights issue of one share for every eight held at 6.00 ringgit per share.

The issue of 67.56 million shares is expected to net around 405.4 million ringgit which would be used to increase the status of the bank as well as to fund future expansion, the bank said in a statement to the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange.

"The proceeds would be used ... to expand the capital base of the bank towards achieving Tier-1 capital requirements, to meet the capital requirements of its subdidiary, Hong Leong Finance Bhd, and for future expansion purposes," Hong Leong Bank said.
Malaysia's central bank introduced a two-tier banking system in late 1995, whereby Tier-1 banks enjoy greater regulatory freedom.
Tier-1 banks are also required to have minimum shareholders' funds of 500 million ringgit, which should be increased to one billion ringgit in the next few years.
